claims.claim: Katelyn Beecroft captured the Moon occulting Jupiter on Oct. 6, 2026 using an 8-inch Dobsonian reflector and ZWO ASI224MC camera from London, Ontario.
claims.episode_span: Katelyn Beecroft in London, Ontario captured the event on the morning of Oct. 6, 2026. The waning crescent Moon, about 20 percent lit, passed in front of Jupiter. She tracked by hand with an 8-inch Dobsonian reflector. Video came from a ZWO ASI224MC planetary camera.
claims.supporting_quote: On the morning of Oct. 6, 2026, the waning crescent Moon — then about 20 percent lit — occulted Jupiter as seen from much of eastern North America. This imager, tracking by hand with an 8-inch Dobsonian reflector, stacked the sharpest frames from video shot with a ZWO ASI224MC planetary camera.

claims.claim: LOFAR produced a radio image showing almost 63,000 sources across a sky patch 25 times the area of the full Moon.
claims.episode_span: The image shows almost 63,000 radio sources including active galactic nuclei and star-forming galaxies. Results were accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics and are available on arXiv.
claims.source_title: Astronomers deliver the sharpest and deepest view yet of the low-frequency radio sky
claims.supporting_quote: Using the Low Frequency Array (LOFAR), an international team led by Leiden University has produced the sharpest and most sensitive radio image of the sky ever made at low radio frequencies. The image reveals almost 63,000 radio sources, such as active galactic nuclei and star-forming galaxies, across a patch of sky about 25 times the area of the full moon.

claims.claim: Swift re-entered on November 4 at 7:39 EST over North Sumatra after nearly 22 years of service.
claims.episode_span: NASA’s Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory re-entered Earth’s atmosphere on November 4 at 7:39 EST over the North Sumatra region of Indonesia. The satellite had operated for nearly 22 years.
claims.source_title: APOD: 2026 November 6 – A Farewell to Swift
claims.supporting_quote: After nearly 22 years of service, the satellite re-entered Earth’s atmosphere on November 4 at 7:39 EST over the North Sumatra region of Indonesia.
